subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs VendorX & ModelCo (OmniHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs VendorX & ModelCo (OmniHealth)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today to run through OmniHealth's evaluation criteria and the demo. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the key takeaways, how Redwood stacks up vs. the other vendors in the bake-off, and propose next steps. Attaching a short summary PDF and a test-plan CSV with the sample prompts you provided.

1) Primary pain points you confirmed:
- High 95th % latency on burst inference for patient-facing workflows (goal < 200ms).
- Cost unpredictability across peak hours; looking to reduce per-session token cost.
- Data residency and auditability requirements for PHI-adjacent logs.

2) Goals for the proof-of-concept / bake-off:
- Latency: 95th % < 200ms for typical 256-token responses under expected traffic profile.
- Quality: match or exceed current vendor (ModelCo) on NPS-style accuracy for triage responses.
- Controls: customer-managed key support (KMS), retention retention policy controls, and audit logs.

3) Quick vendor comparison (high level):
- Redwood: strong on latency controls (dedicated pools + autoscaling), configurable KV caching to reduce repeated prompts, transparent per-route cost breakdowns. We support VPC/private deployments for residency, and can provide SOC2 evidence.
- VendorX: good pricing on published tiers but had higher variabilty in our latency tests during burst. Limited private-deployment story.
- ModelCo: good quality benchmarks on generic tasks; primary limitation is that dedicated capacity is expensive and we saw tokenization/UI integration issues in your prompts.

4) Open questions you asked us to confirm:
- Can Redwood provide a staging tenant in your US region with KMS integration? (yes, we can).
- Can we guarantee snapshot-level audit logs for the duration of the POC? (we can provide audit logs and configurable retention; we'll surface exact retention options).
- Cost estimate for 1M tokens/month with expected batching patterns (we'll provide an estimate based on your session distribution).

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: run the 48-hour bake-off test (included in attached CSV) against a dedicated pool. We provision a test tenant and provide access to logs. (Action: Redwood — Aditya to provision test environment).
- OmniHealth: share final 3 test prompts and a sample traffic shape for a typical 2-hour peak. (Action: Elena).
- Timeline: propose test window next Tue/Wed (2026-04-28/29).

Attachments:
- redwood-omnihealth-bakeoff-summary.pdf (summary + perf charts)
- bakeoff-test-plan.csv (scripts/prompts + pass/fail criteria)

If that matches your read, I'll get Aditya to spin up the environment and we can lock the test window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Elena Morales <elena@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@vendorx.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@modelco.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs VendorX & ModelCo (OmniHealth)

Marissa, thanks for the thorough recap and the attachments, very helpful. A few quick points from our side after an internal read: 

- The latency goal of <200ms 95th feels right for our front-line triage flows. We will provide traffic shape and the 3 prompts by EOD Friday (2026-04-24).
- Can you confirm whether the test tenant will support KMS keys we own (not just customer-managed in name)? We need to ensure we can rotate keys according to our policy.
- Pricing: please include an estimate for both hosted (pay-as-you-go) and dedicated pool pricing for the test volume. Our procurement lead will want a line item.
- One more ask: can Redwood include an initial comparison of tokenization differences between Redwood models and ModelCo for our prompts? We saw some differences in token counts that affect cost.

Also looping in Priya and Tom for visibility — no action required from them yet.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director of Product — OmniHealth
elena@omnihealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs VendorX & ModelCo (internal)

Quick internal notes / answers to Elena's questions so we're aligned before we reply:

- KMS: we support customer-supplied keys via AWS KMS/HSM for the Private deployment and Dedicated can be configured to use a customer key in the cloud region. For hosted test tenant we can enable a customer KMS key scoped to the tenant — confirm with infra, but this is standard. (Action: Aditya to open infra ticket to attach key).
- Tokenization: we should run Elena's 3 prompts through our tokenizer and ModelCo's publicly available tokenizer to produce a per-prompt token delta. I can run that once they send the prompts. (Action: Aditya).
- Test infra: I'll provision a dedicated pool with 2x small GPU nodes to simulate concurrency and enable KV caching. We'll collect 95/99 latency and trace spans.
- Cost estimate: we'll produce a line-item pricing deck (hosted vs dedicated) for 1M, 5M, and 10M token buckets. Tentative ballpark attached to the reply to Elena.

Jordan — FYI on the infrastructure ask and audit log retention requirements; we may need a short paper to satisfy procurement. Rishi — can you prepare a SOC2 / audit-log snippet for Elena?

Thanks,
Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs VendorX & ModelCo (OmniHealth)

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the quick turn. Short answers below and next actions so we can lock the window: 

- KMS: confirmed — we can enable customer-supplied KMS for the hosted test tenant in the US region for the duration of the POC. Key rotation by OmniHealth is supported; we'll need the key ARN beforehand.
- Tokenization: Aditya will run tokenization diffs as soon as you share the three prompts — he'll send a small CSV with token counts for Redwood and ModelCo.
- Pricing: attached is a short estimate (line items for hosted vs dedicated for 1M/5M/10M tokens). Note that dedicated pricing assumes reserved capacity for the two-week window; we'll prorate as needed.
- Audit logs / SOC2 evidence: Rishi will share the SOC2 summary + an audit-log sample and retention controls (cc'd).

Proposed test schedule: provision on Mon (2026-04-27), run Tue/Wed (2026-04-28/29). Can you confirm the Tue/Wed window? Once confirmed, Aditya will provision and share credentials + Grafana links.

Open items for Elena to confirm:
- Provide the 3 prompts and a sample traffic shape by 2026-04-24 EOD.
- Provide KMS key ARN by 2026-04-26.

If that's all good, we'll treat the next reply as confirmation and proceed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
